newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bankers awaiting bondholder plan.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bankers awaiting bondholder plan.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's bondholders are not likely to confer with the company's bankers until the bondholders complete their due diligence of the comic book publisher in the next few weeks, people close to the bondholders said on Wednesday.
The bondholders, led by Carl Ichan, may need about two weeks to complete their due diligence before filing a formal plan for Marvel's reorganization to a bankruptcy court, the people added.

That lack of communication, however, has reportedly so angered Marvel's bankers that they hired the entertainment investment-banking firm Allen & Co to advise them about their options regarding Marvel, the Wall Street Journal said.

The bankers, led by Chase Manhattan Bank, could stand to lose an important source of repayment on their $630 million in Marvel bank debt if the bondholders' plan -- which may result in them keeping an equity stake in Marvel -- is approved. Among the banks' options, the paper reported, was to file their own reorganization plan.
Such a plan could put financier Ronald Perelman, or his Andrews Group, back in control of Marvel, the paper said.
Chase Manhattan Bank had no comment on the report. Officials from Allen & Co could not be immediately reached to comment.

Last Friday, Marvel, which filed for bankruptcy in December, agreed to consider the bondholders' plan to reorganize the company. The bondholders claimed victory at the time in their battle with Perelman, as Perelman's group withdrew its competing reorganization plan and said it supported Marvel's decision to work with the bondholders.
"Marvel's management has been authorized by its board to work with the bondholders to come up with a definitive proposal, and is proceeding accordingly," a Marvel spokesman said on Wednesday.
